input.title: Where should carts live: Redis or Postgres?
input.body:
Carts outgrow the 4 KB session cookie and get truncated. Move cart contents server-side and keep only an opaque cart ID in the cookie.

- **Redis:** sub-millisecond reads, TTL-based expiry suits abandoned carts, and the data model is simple. Costs: another service to run and back up, and cart data is lost on eviction or a misconfigured persistence setting unless you configure it.
- **Postgres:** carts survive restarts and are queryable for abandoned-cart reports. You likely already run it, so there is no new infra. Costs: slightly slower writes on every cart change, and expiry needs a cleanup job.

Recommendation: Postgres, unless you already operate Redis and need very high cart-write volume.

actions.label: Use Postgres (Recommended)
actions.prompt: Store carts in Postgres; keep only a cart ID in the cookie.

actions.prompt: Store carts in Redis with TTL expiry; keep only a cart ID in the cookie.
